data.name: Surajpal
data.gender_notes: Surajpal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Surajpal is a compound name derived from two Sanskrit words: ‘Suraj’ meaning ‘Sun God’ and ‘Pal’ meaning ‘power’. This name is a tribute to the Sun God and signifies the strength and power that comes from him. The name Surajpal carries the meaning “Sun God's Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Surajpal usually hope their child will grow to embody sun god's power and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that connects one to the divine power of the Sun, symbolizing energy, strength, and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Surajpal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun God's Power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Surajpal total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Surajpal reverberates with the rich cultural heritage of India. In ancient Indian philosophy, the Sun God was believed to be the giver of life, energy, and vitality, and the protecter of dharma and justice. Honoring this revered deity by naming a child Surajpal strengthens the cultural bonds and spiritual roots.
data.spiritual_significance: Surajpal draws inspiration from the divinity of the Sun God. It symbolizes inner illumination and enlightenment. The spiritual significance of the name leans towards personal strength, courage, and self-confidence drawn from the divine power of the Sun God. Surajpal is also known to evoke feelings of deep connection to the divine and pursuit of spiritual knowledge and growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Surajpal derived from Sanskrit words 'Surya' (Sun) and 'Pal' (Friend), signifies a friend of the Sun God, symbolizing radiance, warmth, and the power to illuminate one's path.

vedic_reference.note: Surajpal is a name derived from the Sanskrit words सूरज (sūraj, sun) and पाल (pāl, pool, abode). The long meaning 'Sun's Abode' reflects the belief that the sun is a deity and a source of life and energy.

historical_references.reference: Surajpal was a Rajput warrior who defended the Mughal Emperor Jehangir against rebel forces led by Prince Shah Jahan and his father, Asaf Khan. This conflict, known as the 'Eight Years' War', took place from 1622 to 1628.

Later, Surajpal served as the Rajput general under Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, participating in various military campaigns against the Marathas and the Afghans. He is best remembered for his victory over the Marathas at the Battle of Sangamner in 1636.
historical_references.context: Mughal Empire, Military Campaigns against Marathas and Afghans
